items.title: Grid
items.desc: 12 × 98 + 11 × 24 = 1440. There is no outer margin inside the content frame — the 240px on each side is viewport space, not a grid margin.

items.title: Breakpoints
items.desc: Column counts follow the current mainstream convention — four on a handset, eight on a portrait tablet, twelve from laptop width up. Breakpoint boundaries at 600 and 1024 match the

items.title: Typography
items.desc: Two families and eleven styles. Barlow Condensed carries every page and section title, always uppercase; Barlow carries body copy, labels and figures.

items.title: Corner cut
items.desc: The signature shape of the system: a 45° cut on the top-left and bottom-right corner of every surface. All other corners stay square. Border radius is 0 everywhere except flags and

items.title: Outlined variant
items.desc: A CSS border is clipped away along the diagonal, so nothing is painted there and the cut disappears. Every outlined surface is built as two layers.

items.title: Stroke
items.desc: The four brand colours drawn as a single angular gradient around the edge of a surface. It is the one place all four appear at once, so it is reserved for a single hero container p

items.title: ctl-01 Button
items.desc: Primary is a solid black surface — there is no coloured brand button in this system. All three variants share one geometry so they swap by property alone. Focus is a 2px black ring

items.title: ctl-02 Link
items.desc: Uppercase and black, with no underline at rest — the arrow carries the affordance. The rule only appears on hover and focus, so a page full of links stays quiet.

items.title: ctl-03 Tab
items.desc: The selected tab is a filled black block with a white label, notched on the top-left corner only so it sits flush on the rule beneath the strip. Same selection treatment as el-02 GenderSwitch.

items.title: ctl-07 WatchLive
items.desc: The link out to the YouTube stream. There is no video module in this system — the league streams on YouTube and the site sends people there, so the only thing to design is the butt

items.title: ctl-04 Input & Select
items.desc: Focus is a 2px ring outside the field rather than a thicker border, so the field never shifts by a pixel when focused.

items.title: ctl-05 Checkbox
items.desc: Used for the region and category filters where several values can be active at once.

items.title: ctl-08 ToggleSwitch
items.desc: One switch for a view that filters itself. Not a checkbox — ctl-05 adds a value to a set, this changes what the table in front of you is. Outlined when off, solid black when on.

items.title: ctl-06 Pagination
items.desc: Only on the full standings view. Everything else uses Load more.

items.title: el-16 Card
items.desc: The generic content container. News, photos, conferences and team entries are all this component with a different body — one geometry, one set of states, one shadow scale.

items.title: el-01 SectionHeader
items.desc: Title plus an optional action link. No mark, no rule — secondary branding is carried by the wording itself ("Nations League + section") rather than by a graphic device, so the head

items.title: el-02 GenderSwitch
items.desc: Rebuilt without a grey track. Two outlined segments sit directly on the page and share a 1px border; the active one fills black. That removes a nesting level and lets the control d

items.title: el-14 Chip
items.desc: The text-only sibling of el-13. One component covers the region filter bar, the applied-filter tokens and any inline tag, so there is only ever one chip geometry in the system.

items.title: el-03 FilterChips
items.desc: Region filter — a row of el-14 Chip at size M. "AsiaPacific" is one word: that is the agreed naming rule, not a typo.

items.title: el-33 FilterDrawer
items.desc: One trigger for every filter on a page; the panel holds chips, selects and the toggle.

items.title: el-05 StatusBadge
items.desc: Six states, one geometry. Red is reserved for LIVE and appears nowhere else in the system. Not interactive, so it has no hover or focus.

items.title: el-13 FederationTag
items.desc: The flag and the federation name are one element, not two cells that happen to sit next to each other. Everywhere a federation appears — table row, autocomplete, filter token, team

items.title: el-06 StopDots
items.desc: Replaces the sentence "4 out of 6 stops played". Six or eight items are recognised at a glance without counting, so the dots alone carry it. Two types — a read-only indicator, and

items.title: el-08 TableHeaderRow
items.desc: The header half of the table pair. Every cell width here must equal the matching cell width in el-04 TeamRow — that single rule is what keeps the table aligned, and it is what the

items.title: el-04 TeamRow
items.desc: One row of any standings table. Rows sit directly on the page — there is no card around the table. In Figma this becomes a component with one boolean property per column, so a colu

items.title: el-07 AccordionShell
items.desc: The World Tour drill-down pattern: start at 20,000 feet, expand in place, never leave the page. The expanded body has no fill of its own, so the table sits one level deep, not two.

items.title: el-09 Legend
items.desc: Every abbreviated column needs a one-line explainer. It sits above its table and right-aligned, with a rule on top only — a second rule underneath would fight the table header.

items.title: el-10 EmptyState
items.desc: Not optional. Qualification data is entered by hand and editorial supply is not guaranteed, so every module has to hold its shape with nothing in it. Outlined rather than filled, s

items.title: el-11 SearchInput
items.desc: The gateway built on the assumption that fans look for their own federation and little else. Accepts a name or an IOC code. The suggestion list is a separate component (el-15) so a A clear control appears at the trailing edge as soon as the field has text.

items.title: el-15 AutocompleteMenu
items.desc: The suggestion list that drops out of el-11. It is its own component because the same list appears under the header search, the Find a team module and the conference filter.

items.title: el-18 NavTab
items.desc: One item of the mobile bottom bar. Icon over an uppercase label, with a 2px rule under the active item so the marker matches the desktop navigation exactly.

items.title: el-19 DisclosureRow
items.desc: A compact single-line accordion row. It is what turns the five-column desktop footer into something usable on a phone, and it is reused anywhere a list needs to collapse without th

items.title: el-20 Toast
items.desc: A transient message. It carries the follow reminder, the "a conference just went live" alert, and confirmation after an action.

items.title: el-21 Tooltip
items.desc: The one-line explainer that every abbreviated column in the system is required to carry. Anchored to the header cell, opening below it.

items.title: el-22 CarouselIndicator
items.desc: Position and progress for any carousel. Bars are the default because they double as a progress track; round dots are the compact variant for tight placements.

items.title: el-23 Breadcrumb
items.desc: The path back up. It was living inside F-04 SubHeader; pulling it out means search results, articles and stop pages can all use the same one. Every page states its own trail: pages carrying an entity were leaving the specimen’s text in place.

items.title: el-24 Avatar
items.desc: A player thumbnail for rosters, stat leaderboards, search results and page headers. Two fallbacks, because portraits will not exist for most of the field in year one. XL is 116, wh

items.title: el-25 AlphaIndex
items.desc: The A to Z jump bar. No longer used on the Teams page, where the region filter replaced it.

items.title: el-26 Skeleton
items.desc: The loading state. Every table, card rail and article on this site is populated from an API, and until now none of them had anything to show while that request is in flight.

items.title: el-27 InlineBanner
items.desc: A notice that belongs to the page rather than to a moment. Where el-20 Toast appears and disappears, this stays until the condition it describes is over.

items.title: el-28 ShareMenu
items.desc: Sharing for articles, photos and player pages. The trigger is a ghost button; the menu drops beneath it on e2.

items.title: el-29 AdSpace
items.desc: A reserved advertising slot. It sits mid-page or above the footer, never in the header, and it is drawn as an explicit placeholder so a page never looks broken while a slot is unso

items.title: el-30 CalendarStrip
items.desc: Eight equal days with previous and next at either end. It fills whatever column it is dropped into, so the same component serves the landing page and the calendar page. The eight days are local calendar days; a region with fewer playing days is padded outward, never with a day it already shows.

items.title: F-02 GlobalHeader
items.desc: The FIBA corporate strip above the competition bar. 1920 wide, 34px tall, 8/16 padding, wordmark at 12/18 uppercase, matching the agreed header frame.

items.title: F-03 CompetitionNav
items.desc: The competition bar, following the World Tour pattern: full-bleed black, the mark in a slanted white lozenge on the left, the wordmark beside it, navigation right-aligned, and the

items.title: F-03m CompetitionNav — mobile
items.desc: Two pieces at 390px: a 56px header that carries only the wordmark and search, and a sticky bottom bar with the five destinations that matter. Everything else lives behind More.

items.title: F-04 SubHeader
items.desc: The page identity block: breadcrumb, H1, and context. It is the most contested module in the system — one side of the review reads it as redundant with the navigation, the other de An identity column on the left and a control slot on the right, which is where el-02 GenderSwitch lives on every page.

items.title: F-07 HomeHero
items.desc: Landing page hero band — photo plate, key-visual fragments, lockup and one link.

items.title: F-05 MegaMenu
items.desc: What opens under More. Three columns of destinations plus one featured story, on the same black chrome as the navigation bar so the panel reads as an extension of it rather than as The current page is marked the way F-03 marks it — white label, white rule under it. The gold accent is a hover colour, not a selection.

items.title: F-06 SiteFooter
items.desc: Five columns, the supplier band and the legal row. Official ball sits left, official suppliers right, so the two tiers read as separate groups rather than one

items.title: F-06m SiteFooter — mobile
items.desc: The five desktop columns become five el-19 DisclosureRow accordions, one open at a time. The lockup and social row stay visible at the top; the supplier band wraps

items.title: S-01 LiveConferenceAccordion
items.desc: The landing page answer to "what is happening right now", and to "what happened on the day I just picked". Only live conferences appear by default (LP-14), there is no game list (L The gender switch has moved out of each panel to the filter bar above the strip — one control for the whole block.

items.title: S-02 StopTimeline
items.desc: A conference as six sequential stops. The rule above each stop carries the state — black for played and live, grey for upcoming — and the live stop is marked by the red dot and the

items.title: S-03 CalendarStrip
items.desc: Eight equal days with previous and next controls at either end, sized to fill whatever column it is dropped into. The date leads at 40px, the weekday and month stack beside it, and

items.title: S-04 GameList
items.desc: Games grouped by day, built on exactly the same table as the standings. Federation names open the team page and Box score opens the player-level detail for that game: a header row

items.title: S-12 GameDetail
items.desc: The page behind every Box score link. Score lockup, two team plates, top scorer, box score, match stats and play-by-play. No video: the league streams on YouTube.

items.title: S-05 Pools
items.desc: The pool stage of a stop. A black rule on the left marks the teams that advance, so the cut line is visible without a legend.

items.title: S-06 Bracket
items.desc: The knockout stage. Three formats are in use across the league depending on how many federations enter a stop, so the module is one component with a format property rather than thr

items.title: S-07 SeasonCalendar
items.desc: The Calendar page: the whole season by month, one row per stop. S-03 CalendarStrip is the eight-day window on the landing page; this is the full list behind it.

items.title: S-08 Podium
items.desc: How a stop closes. Three federations, the winner raised and filled black, shown above the pool tables once the final is played.

items.title: S-09 Overview
items.desc: Where the season stands, as the first block of a page. Two types: conferences alone for the landing page, conferences and stops worldwide for the Conferences page. Named Season status until 18 August 2026.

items.title: S-10 SeasonJourney
items.desc: A federation's conference read stop by stop — where it finished, what it was worth, whether it has been played. Sits above the roster on a team page.

items.title: S-11 StopMatrix
items.desc: One row per federation, one column per stop. Johannes’ original, and what Alex asked for on slide 9 — "Good, but show six stops".

items.title: S-13 Countdown
items.desc: The block for a page with nothing to report yet — the league between seasons, or a World Tour / Women's Series stop that has not started. Four counters, a brand variant for a hero band, a compact strip, and a zero state that hands over to the live badge.

items.title: R-01 QualificationBoard
items.desc: The landing page centrepiece and the module the whole redesign turns on. Twenty rows: position, federation, conference, status. Nothing else — this replaced the old Standings block

items.title: R-02 StandingsTable
items.desc: One table, not two. Competition Standings and Qualification are merged and ctl-08 ToggleSwitch cuts the table down to the twenty places that are going.

items.title: R-03 ConferenceStandings
items.desc: The same column logic scoped to one conference, with the winner visually distinguished. The winner highlight was requested specifically, because a conference winner qualifies the m

items.title: R-04 StatLeaders
items.desc: Removed from the landing page (LP-10) and re-homed here. Games played and points per game were both requested, as was a link from every player name to a profile.

items.title: R-05 StatLeaderboard
items.desc: The Stats page: the full field ranked on one metric, with the category chosen above the table. R-04 StatLeaders is the three-column summary that lives on other pages; this is the p

items.title: R-06 SeasonChampions
items.desc: Off-season landing block — conference winners going to the U23 World Cup.

items.title: E-01 TeamFinder
items.desc: The gateway built on a simple assumption: fans look for their own federation and little else. Accepts a name or an IOC code.

items.title: E-02 ConferenceHeader
items.desc: Identity and stop navigation for a conference page. The name carries the age category (Africa East U23), which is why no U23 or U21 column exists anywhere else in the system.

items.title: E-03 ConferenceGrid
items.desc: One card per conference, grouped under a region caption. Federations are named with el-13 FederationTag at size S; the U21 conferences sit inside their region.

items.title: E-04 TeamHeader
items.desc: Federation identity at the top of a team page: flag, name, category, conference, qualification state, and the six numbers that describe the season. The gender switch is not part of this module — it lives in F-04’s control slot. Previously it sa

items.title: E-12 FederationOverview
items.desc: Team page with All selected — one card per category, each linking to its team site.

items.title: E-05 PlayerHeader
items.desc: The header of a single player page — the destination behind every player name in a roster, a box score or a stat leaderboard. Portrait, name, federation, category, the link out to

items.title: E-06 PlayerSeasonStats
items.desc: The season summary and the per-stop breakdown. This is where the Stat Leaders panel removed from the landing page (LP-10) actually lives.

items.title: E-07 GameLog
items.desc: Every game a player has appeared in, newest first: date, conference, opponent, result and the individual line, with links to the clip and the gallery when they exist.

items.title: E-08 PlayerCard
items.desc: The roster tile on a team page. Four stacked layers so the whole set reskins from one background swap: background, cut-out portrait, stat column, name plate. It follows the existin On hover the card lifts, tips slightly towards the pointer and a specular band crosses it.

items.title: E-09 FederationDirectory
items.desc: The Teams index, filtered by region. The A–Z jump bar gave way to a row of el-14 Chip — the region is what people know, not the letter.

items.title: E-10 RosterGrid
items.desc: The squad on a team page, in two views. Cards are the default because the roster is the emotional part of a team page; the list is for anyone comparing numbers.

items.title: E-13 NextGeneration
items.desc: Pre-season landing block — six E-08 player cards per gender.

items.title: E-11 SearchResults
items.desc: The search overlay. It opens over the page rather than navigating to a result page, so a fan never loses where they were; results are grouped by what they are. Federations come fir

items.title: C-01 AboutBlock
items.desc: What replaces the hero. The banner copy was to be removed and the explanation moved into a real About section (LP-02, LP-03), so that a visitor can understand how a team reaches th

items.title: C-02 NewsRail
items.desc: Three stories on the landing page: image, headline, date. One card type only, so a recap generated from results sits beside a written feature without announcing which is which.

items.title: C-03 PhotoGallery
items.desc: Two carousel types plus the viewer. Auto advances on its own with a progress indicator and a pause control, and belongs on the landing page. Manual has previous and next plus a pos

items.title: C-04 NewsList
items.desc: The News index. C-02 NewsRail is the three-card row on the landing page; this is the paginated list behind it, filtered by the same category labels.

items.title: C-05 Article
items.desc: The article page. A hero, a headline block, the byline with sharing, and a body constrained to 830px — seven columns — because that is where line length stays readable.

items.title: C-06 ContentPage
items.desc: The template behind About, How it works and FAQ: a sticky table of contents on the left, long-form body on the right, and el-19 DisclosureRow for anything question-shaped.

items.title: C-07 SignupCTA
items.desc: Off/pre-season e-mail sign-up block.

items.title: C-08 Winners
items.desc: Off-season landing gallery — one prize-ceremony photo per qualified federation.

items.title: S-14 StopBar
items.desc: The season as a submenu. Past recedes, the live stop is the only white one and the only one with a dot, the stops still to come stay legible.

items.title: el-31 MeterBar
items.desc: One value against a track. Stackable, so rows can be compared — which S-09's built-in bar and el-22's filling bar cannot do.

items.title: el-32 VideoThumb
items.desc: A video poster that links out. There is no player in this system; this is the thumbnail that sends people to one.
